residencyRequirements.description: The filing spouse must have lived in Rhode Island for at least one year before filing for divorce.

waitingPeriod.description: Rhode Island has no mandatory waiting period after filing. However, for irreconcilable differences, the plaintiff must make a statement under oath.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences which have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Willful Desertion
fault.description: Willful desertion for five years of either of the parties

fault.name: Drug Addiction
fault.description: Habitual and excessive use of opium, morphine, or chloral or other drug addiction

fault.name: Neglect and Refusal to Provide
fault.description: Neglect and refusal of the husband to provide necessaries for the subsistence of his wife

fault.name: Living Separate for Three Years
fault.description: Living separate and apart without cohabitation for at least three years

fault.name: Gross Misbehavior
fault.description: Gross misbehavior and wickedness repugnant to and in violation of the marriage covenant

groundsForDissolution.notes: Rhode Island has both fault and no-fault grounds. The most common ground is irreconcilable differences (no-fault). Rhode Island uses 'Complaint for Divorce' not 'Petition'.

propertyDivision.description: Rhode Island courts divide marital property equitably. The court considers factors including the length of the marriage, the conduct of the parties during the marriage, the contribution of each party to the acquisition, preservation, or appreciation of assets, and the needs of the custodial parent.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before the marriage or by inheritance or gift may be considered separate property, but the court has discretion to include it in the distribution.

filingFees.notes: Rhode Island filing fees are approximately $160. Fee waivers may be available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Statement (DR-6)
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, expenses, and debts

basic.name: Final Judgment of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Rhode Island Family Court Child Support Guidelines

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Rhode Island Family Court Rules

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Rhode Island has 30 days to file an answer

responseDeadlines.statute: R.I. Super. Ct. R. Civ. P. 12(a)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Rhode Island uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Rhode Island Family Court Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if strict application would be inequitable.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Rhode Island courts may award alimony after considering factors including the length of the marriage, the conduct of the parties, the health and age of each party, the ability of each party to support themselves, and the contribution of each party to the marriage.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available based on need and ability to pay. No formula-based calculation.

court.name: Family Court
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Family Court. (R.I. Gen. Laws §8-10-1 et seq.)
